field.label: Enable
field.help: Run the CARP failover helpers on this node. The same settings belong on both nodes; HA sync carries them when "CARP failover helpers" is ticked in the sync settings.

field.label: Reference CARP address
field.help: The LAN-side CARP virtual IP whose state (MASTER or BACKUP) decides the role of this node. The backup node also reaches the internet through this address. Nothing happens until one is selected.

field.label: Boot grace
field.help: Seconds after boot during which a MASTER event is not trusted while the pfsync peer still answers: a booting node can time out to MASTER before it hears the real master.

field.label: Backup egress
field.help: On the BACKUP node, route 0.0.0.0/1 and 128.0.0.0/1 through the master's CARP address so the node itself has internet (updates, NTP, blocklists). With os-carp-vip-dhcp installed, leave its own "Backup egress" unticked on every keeper.

field.label: Pin default route
field.help: Keep the kernel default route on a usable upstream gateway and on that gateway's device, on both roles. Gateway monitoring cannot probe through the CARP addresses on a backup, so OPNsense may leave no default route there; a takeover would then forward nothing until the monitors recover. With os-carp-vip-dhcp installed, set its "Own default route by CARP role" to Off on every keeper.

field.label: Unusable default gateways
field.help: Address patterns (shell wildcards) of a default gateway that is not one of the configured upstream gateways and must be re-pinned, for example a LAN address left behind. A configured upstream gateway is always accepted, even a private one.

field.label: Gateway ping timeout
field.help: Milliseconds to wait for an upstream gateway to answer when picking one on a new master.

field.label: Peer ping timeout
field.help: Milliseconds to wait for the pfsync peer to answer on the sync link.

field.label: Routing delay
field.help: Seconds a CARP or boot event waits before the routes are reconciled, so the role has settled.

field.label: Lock timeout
field.help: Seconds a run waits for an earlier run to finish: one CARP transition fires the hooks once per address.

field.label: Restart Unbound on takeover
field.help: Restart Unbound when this node becomes MASTER of the reference address, so it drops upstream failures it cached as backup, then check that it resolves.

field.label: Check name
field.help: Name resolved to verify Unbound after the restart.

field.label: Check server
field.help: Resolver queried for the check.

field.label: Restart attempts
field.help: How often Unbound is restarted when the check fails.

field.label: Settle time
field.help: Seconds to wait before the first restart, so the routes are in place.

field.label: Check delay
field.help: Seconds to wait after each restart before checking.

field.label: Services
field.help: Services that must run on the master only, for example miniupnpd, udpbroadcastrelay or ddclient, as listed under System: Diagnostics: Services (the list offers the services of this node; other names can be typed). They are started on MASTER and stopped otherwise, on CARP events, at boot and every two minutes. Enable each service on both nodes.

field.label: Settle time
field.help: Seconds to wait after a start or stop before checking that it took.

field.label: Event delay
field.help: Seconds a CARP event waits before the services (and the Tailscale handover) are reconciled.

field.label: Boot delay
field.help: Seconds after boot before the services are reconciled.

field.label: Tailscale nodes
field.help: Tailscale host names of both nodes when both advertise the same subnets. Tailscale keeps the routes on whichever node had them first; the backup then stops tailscaled for a moment so they move to the master. Empty turns this off. If Tailscale is the only way in to a node, keep another one.

field.label: Handover hold
field.help: Seconds tailscaled stays stopped on the backup during a handover.

field.label: pfsync maxupd
field.help: Value set on pfsync0 at boot (0 leaves pfsync alone). A low value keeps the standby state windows fresh so TCP connections survive a planned failover. Changing it on a running MASTER causes a short CARP flip, so it is applied there at the next boot only.

field.label: Jumbo MTU interfaces
field.help: Devices (not interface names) forced to the jumbo MTU at boot, for example a disabled parent interface and the VLAN on it whose MTU OPNsense does not apply. A device that carries an upstream gateway is refused.

field.label: Jumbo MTU
field.help: MTU set on those devices.
